label: myadhd.my
caption:
Lunch? It is 4pm.

Forgetting to eat, drink or even stretch is common with ADHD. Swipe for why your body's signals get lost, and three ways to catch them sooner.

If this sounded like your brain, come sit with people who get it. Our group is in my bio 👇

Save this, then go drink some water.

#adhd #adhdmalaysia #myadhd #adhdadult #adhdtips

slides.title:
Why do I
forget to
[[eat]]?
slides.sub: You are not careless with yourself. The signal is just quiet.

slides.title:
Your body's
signals arrive
[[quietly]]
slides.body: Hungry, thirsty, needing the toilet, needing to move. Most people notice early. For many ADHD brains, those signals stay faint until they are urgent.

slides.title:
Focus turns
the volume
[[down]] more
slides.body: Deep in something interesting, you will not hear your stomach at all. You look up, it is dark, and you have had one coffee.

slides.title:
Then it hits
[[all at once]]
slides.body: Shaky, snappy, a headache out of nowhere. You do not feel a little hungry. You go from fine to starving in a minute.

slides.title:
Hungry looks
like a [[mood]]
slides.body: Irritable, foggy, close to tears. It is easy to blame yourself or the day. Often the first thing to try is food and water.

slides.title:
Eat by the
[[clock]], not
the feeling
slides.body: If the signal is unreliable, do not wait for it. A lunch alarm at 1pm does the noticing for you.

slides.title:
Keep food
where you
[[already are]]
slides.body: A snack on the desk, a bottle of water by the laptop. If eating needs a trip to the kitchen, focus will win every time.

slides.title:
Make [[easy]]
food count
slides.body: Toast, fruit, a boiled egg, yesterday's rice. On a busy day, a simple meal eaten beats a good meal planned.

slides.title:
Save this, then
go drink some
[[water]]
slides.body: Your body is not quiet because it needs nothing. Dump today into my.adhd and get one thing back, after you eat.
